paragraphs.sourceText: The Three-Year Solution
paragraphs.translationZh: 三年解决方案

paragraphs.sourceText: Hartwick College, a small liberal-arts school in upstate New York, makes New York, makes this offer to well prepared students: earn your undergraduate degree in three years instead of four, and save about 543,000—the amount of one year’s tuition and fees. A number of innovative colleges are making the same offer to students anxious about saving time and money. That’s both an opportunity and a warning for the best higher-education system in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈特威克学院是纽约州北部的一所小型文理学院，为准备充分的学生提供了这样的优惠：在三年而不是四年内获得本科学位，并节省约 543,000 美元——相当于一年的学杂费。许多创新型大学也向渴望节省时间和金钱的学生提供同样的优惠。对于世界上最好的高等教育体系来说，这既是机遇，也是警告。

paragraphs.sourceText: The United States has almost all of the world’s best universities. A recent Chinese survey ranks 35 American universities among the top 50, eight among the top 10. Our research universities have been the key to developing the competitive advantages that help Americans produce 25% of all the world’s wealth. In 2007, 623,805 of the world’s brightest students were attracted to American universities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国几乎拥有世界上所有最好的大学。中国最近的一项调查将 35 所美国大学列入前 50 名，其中 8 所大学进入前 10 名。我们的研究型大学一直是发展竞争优势的关键，帮助美国人创造了全球 25% 的财富。 2007年，全球有623,805名最聪明的学生被美国大学吸引。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet, there are signs of peril (危险)within American higher education. U.S. colleges have to compete in the marketplace. Students may choose among 6,000 public, private, nonprofit, for profit, or religious institutions of higher learning. In addition, almost all of the 532 billion the federal government provides for university research is awarded competitively.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，美国高等教育中存在危险的迹象。美国大学必须在市场上竞争。学生可以在 6,000 所公立、私立、非营利、营利或宗教高等院校中进行选择。此外，联邦政府为大学研究提供的5320亿美元几乎全部都是竞争性拨款。

paragraphs.sourceText: But many colleges and universities are stuck in the past. For instance, the idea of the fall-to-spring“school year”hasn’t changed much since before the American Revolution, when we were a summer stretch no longer makes sense. Former George Washington University president Stephen Trachtenberg estimates that a typical college uses its facilities for academic purposes a little more than half the calendar year.“While college facilities sit idle, they continue to generate maintenance expenses that contribute to the high cost of running a college,” he has written.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但许多学院和大学还停留在过去。例如，从秋季到春季的“学年”的概念自美国革命之前以来就没有太大变化，当时我们处于夏季阶段已经不再有意义。乔治华盛顿大学前校长史蒂芬·特拉亨伯格估计，一所典型的大学每年有一半多的时间将其设施用于学术目的。“虽然大学设施闲置，但它们仍然会产生维护费用，从而导致学院的运营成本很高，”他写道。

paragraphs.sourceText: Within academic departments, tenure(终身职位)，combined with age-discrimination laws, makes faculty turnover—critical for a university to remain current in changing times—difficult. Instead of protecting speech and encouraging diversity and innovative thinking, the tenure system often stifles(压制)them: younger professors must win the approval of established colleagues for tenure, encouraging like-mindedness and sometimes inhibiting the free flow of ideas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在学术部门内，终身职位与年龄歧视法相结合，使得教师流动变得困难——这对于大学在不断变化的时代中保持与时俱进至关重要。终身教授制度非但没有保护言论、鼓励多样性和创新思维，反而经常压制他们：年轻的教授必须赢得老同事的认可才能获得终身教授职位，鼓励志同道合，有时会抑制思想的自由流动。

paragraphs.sourceText: Meanwhile, tuition has soared, leaving graduating students with unprecedented loan debt. Strong campus presidents to manage these problems are becoming harder to find, and to keep. In
paragraphs.translationZh: 与此同时，学费飙升，使即将毕业的学生背负着前所未有的贷款债务。能够解决这些问题的强有力的校园校长变得越来越难找到和留住。在

paragraphs.sourceText: fact, students now stay on campus almost as long as their presidents. The average amount of time students now take to complete an undergraduate degree has stretched to six years and seven months as students interrupted by work, inconvenienced by unavailable classes, or lured by one more football season find it hard to graduate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，学生们现在在校园里呆的时间几乎和他们的校长一样长。现在，学生完成本科学位的平均时间已延长至六年零七个月，因为学生因工作而中断、因无法上课而造成不便，或因又一个足球赛季而难以毕业。

paragraphs.sourceText: Congress has tried to help students with college costs through Pell Grants and other forms of tuition support. But some of their fixes have made the problem worse. The stack of congressional regulations governing federal student grants and loans now stands twice as tall as I do. Filling out these forms consumes 7% of every tuition dollar.
paragraphs.translationZh: 国会试图通过佩尔助学金和其他形式的学费支持来帮助学生支付大学费用。但他们的一些修复措施使问题变得更糟。现在，国会管理联邦学生助学金和贷款的法规是我的两倍高。填写这些表格花费了每一美元学费的 7%。

paragraphs.sourceText: For all of these reasons, some colleges like Hartwick are rethinking the old way of doing things and questioning decades-old assumptions about what a college degree means. For instance, why does it have to take four years to earn a diploma? This fall, 16 first-year students and four second-year students at Hartwick enrolled in the school’s new three year degree program. According to the college, the plan is designed for high-ability, highly motivated student who wish to save money or to move along more rapidly toward advanced degrees.
paragraphs.translationZh: 出于所有这些原因，像哈特威克大学这样的一些大学正在重新思考旧的做事方式，并对几十年前关于大学学位含义的假设提出质疑。例如，为什么需要四年才能获得文凭？今年秋天，哈特威克大学的 16 名一年级学生和 4 名二年级学生报名参加了学校新的三年制学位课程。据该学院称，该计划是为那些希望省钱或更快地攻读高级学位的高能力、积极性高的学生而设计的。

paragraphs.sourceText: By eliminating that extra year, there year degree students save 25% in costs. Instead of taking 30 credits a year, these students take 40. During January, Hartwick runs a four week course during which students may earn three to four credits on or off campus, including a number of international sites. Summer courses are not required, but a student may enroll in them—and pay extra. Three year students get first crack at course registration. There are no changes in the number of courses professors teach or in their pay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 通过消除额外的一年，该年级学位学生可以节省 25% 的费用。这些学生不是每年修读 30 个学分，而是修读 40 个学分。一月份，Hartwick 开设为期四周的课程，在此期间，学生可以在校内或校外（包括许多国际站点）获得三到四个学分。暑期课程不是必需的，但学生可以报名参加，并支付额外费用。三年级学生首先可以注册课程。教授教授的课程数量或薪酬没有变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: The three-year degree isn’t a new idea. Geniuses have always breezed through. Judson College, a 350-student institution in Alabama, has offered students a three-year option for 40 years. Students attend “short terms” in May and June to earn the credits required for graduation. Bates College in Maine and Ball State University in Indiana are among other colleges offering three-year options.
paragraphs.translationZh: 三年制学位并不是一个新想法。天才总是轻而易举地走过来的。贾德森学院是阿拉巴马州的一所拥有 350 名学生的机构，为学生提供为期 40 年的三年制选择。学生在五月和六月参加“短期课程”以获得毕业所需的学分。缅因州的贝茨学院和印第安纳州的鲍尔州立大学是其他提供三年制选择的大学之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Changes at the high-school level are also helping to make it easier for many students to earn their undergraduate degrees in less time. One of five students arrives at college today with Advanced Placement (AP) credits amounting to a semester or more of college level work. Many universities, including large schools like the University of Texas, make it easy for these AP students to graduate faster.
paragraphs.translationZh: 高中阶段的变化也有助于让许多学生更容易在更短的时间内获得本科学位。今天，五名学生中就有一名获得大学先修课程 (AP) 学分，相当于一个学期或更长的大学水平课程。许多大学，包括德克萨斯大学等大型学校，都让这些 AP 学生可以轻松更快地毕业。

paragraphs.sourceText: For students who don’t plan to stop with an undergraduate degree, the three-year plan may have an even greater appeal. Dr. John Sergent, head of Vanderbilt University Medical School’s residency (住院医生) program, enrolled in Vanderbilt’s undergraduate college in 1959. He entered medical school after only three years as did four or five of his classmates.” My first year of medical school counted as my senior year, which meant I had to take three to four labs a week to get all my sciences in. I basically skipped my senior year,” says Sergent. He still had time to be a student senator and meet his wife.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于那些不打算停止获得本科学位的学生来说，三年计划可能更具吸引力。约翰·瑟金特博士是范德比尔特大学医学院住院医生项目的负责人，1959年就读于范德比尔特大学本科学院。仅仅三年后，他就和他的四五个同学一样进入了医学院。我在医学院的第一年算作我的高年级，这意味着我每周必须参加三到四个实验室才能学习所有的科学知识。我基本上跳过了高年级，”Sergent 说。他还有时间成为一名学生参议员并见到他的妻子。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are, however, drawbacks to moving through school at such a brisk pace. For one, it deprives students of the luxury of time to roam (遨游) intellectually. Compressing everything into three years also leaves less time for growing up, engaging in extracurricular activities, and studying abroad. On crowded campuses it could mean fewer opportunities to get into a prized professor’s class. Iowa’s Waldorf College has graduated several hundred students in its three-year degree program, but it now phasing out the option. Most Waldorf students wanted the full four-year experience—academically, socially, and athletically. And faculty members will be wary of any change that threatens the core curriculum in the name of moving students into the workforce.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，以如此快的速度完成学业也有一些缺点。其一，它剥夺了学生进行智力漫游的奢侈时间。把一切都压缩在三年里，也让成长、参加课外活动和出国留学的时间变得更少。在拥挤的校园里，这可能意味着进入知名教授班级的机会更少。爱荷华州华尔道夫学院的三年制学位课程已有数百名学生毕业，但现在正在逐步取消该选项。大多数华德福学生都希望获得完整的四年体验——学术、社交和运动方面。教师们将对任何以让学生进入劳动力市场为名威胁核心课程的变化保持警惕。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Most high governmental officials seem to conceive of education in this light—as a way to ensure economic competitiveness and continued economic growth,” Derek Bok, former president of Harvard, told The Washington Post. “I strongly disagree with this approach.” Another risk: the new campus schedules might eventually produce less revenue for the institution and longer working hours for faculty members.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈佛大学前校长德里克·博克 (Derek Bok) 告诉《华盛顿邮报》：“大多数政府高级官员似乎都从这个角度来看待教育，将其视为确保经济竞争力和持续经济增长的一种方式。” “我强烈不同意这种做法。”另一个风险是：新的校园时间表最终可能会减少该机构的收入，并延长教职员工的工作时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: Adopting a three-year option will not come easily to most school. Those that wish to tackle tradition and make American campus more cost-conscious may find it easier to take Trachtenberg’s advice: open campuses year-round.“You could run two complete colleges, with two complete faculties,”he says.“That’s without cutting the length of students’ vacations, increasing class sizes, or requiring faculty to teach more.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于大多数学校来说，采用三年制的选择并不容易。那些希望打破传统、让美国校园更具成本意识的人可能会发现更容易接受特拉亨伯格的建议：全年开放校园。“你可以经营两所完整的大学，拥有两个完整的院系，”他说。“这不需要缩短学生的假期时间，增加班级规模，也不需要教师教授更多的知识。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Whether they experiment with three-year degrees, offer year-round classes, challenge the tenure system—or all of the above—universities are slowly realizing that to stay competitive and relevant they must adapt to a rapidly changing world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无论是尝试三年制学位、提供全年课程、挑战终身教职制度，还是以上所有的大学都在慢慢意识到，为了保持竞争力和相关性，它们必须适应快速变化的世界。

paragraphs.sourceText: Expanding the three-year option may be difficult, but it may be less difficult than asking Congress for additional financial help, asking legislators for more state support, or asking students 4 / 39 even higher tuition payments. Campuses willing to adopt convenient schedules along with more focused, less-expensive degrees may find that they have a competitive advantage in attracting bright, motivated students. These sorts of innovations can help American universities avoid the perils of success.
paragraphs.translationZh: 扩大三年的选择可能很困难，但这可能比要求国会提供额外的财政援助、要求立法者提供更多的国家支持或要求学生支付更高的学费要容易一些。愿意采用便利的时间表以及更专注、更便宜的学位的校园可能会发现它们在吸引聪明、积极的学生方面具有竞争优势。这类创新可以帮助美国大学避免成功的危险。

paragraphs.sourceText: In face of global warming, much effort has been focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions through a variety of strategies. But while much of the research and innovation has
concentrated on finding less-polluting energy alternatives, it may be decades before clean technologies like wind and solar meet a significant portion of our energy needs.

In the meantime, the amount of CO2 in the air is rapidly approaching the limits proposed by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). “As long as we’re consuming fossil fuels, we’re putting out CO2,”says Klaus Lackner, a geophysicist at Columbia, University” We cannot let the CO2 in the atmosphere rise indefinitely.”

That sense of urgency has increased interest in capturing and storing CO2, which the IPCC says could provide the more than 50% reduction in emissions thought needed to reduce global warming.“We see the potential for capture and storage to play an integral role in reducing emissions,” says Kim Corley, Shell’s senior advisor of CO2 and environmental affairs. That forward thinking strategy is gaining support. The U.S. Department of Energy recently proposed putting $1 billion into a new $2.4 billion coal-burning energy plant. The plant’s carbon-capture technologies would serve as a pilot project for other new coal-burning plants.

paragraphs.sourceText: As anyone who has tried to lose weight knows, realistic goal-setting generally produces the best results. That's partially because it appears people who set realistic goals actually work more efficiently, and exert more effort, to achieve those goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 任何尝试过减肥的人都知道，设定现实的目标通常会产生最好的结果。部分原因是，设定现实目标的人实际上工作效率更高，并付出更多努力来实现这些目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: What's far less understood by scientists, however, are the potentially harmful effects of goal-setting.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，科学家们对目标设定的潜在有害影响知之甚少。

paragraphs.sourceText: Newspapers relay daily accounts of goal-setting prevalent in industries and businesses up and down both Wall Street and Main Street , yet there has been surprisingly little research on how the long-trumpeted practice of setting goals may have contributed to the current economic crisis , and unethical (不道德的)behavior in general.
paragraphs.translationZh: 报纸每天都会报道华尔街和大街上各个行业和企业普遍存在的目标设定问题，但令人惊讶的是，对于长期宣扬的设定目标的做法可能如何导致当前的经济危机以及一般的不道德（不道德）行为的研究却很少。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Goals are widely used and promoted as having really beneficial effects. And yet, the same motivation that can push people to exert more effort in a constructive way could also motivate people to be more likely to engage in unethical behaviors,” says Maurice Schweitzer, an associate professor at Penn’s Wharton School.
paragraphs.translationZh: “目标被广泛使用和宣传，因为它具有真正有益的效果。然而，同样的动机可以促使人们以建设性的方式付出更多努力，但也可能会促使人们更有可能做出不道德的行为，”宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院副教授莫里斯·施韦策（Maurice Schweitzer）说。

paragraphs.sourceText: “It turns out there’s no economic benefit to just having a goal---you just get a psychological benefit” Schweitzer says. “But in many cases, goals have economic rewards that make them more powerful.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “事实证明，仅仅有一个目标并没有经济上的好处——你只会得到心理上的好处，”施韦策说。 “但在许多情况下，目标会带来经济回报，从而使其变得更加强大。”

paragraphs.sourceText: A prime example Schweitzer and his colleagues cite is the 2004 collapse of energy-trading giant Enron, where managers used financial incentives to motivate salesmen to meet specific revenue goals. The problem, Schweitzer says, is the actual trades were not profitable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 施韦策和他的同事们引用的一个典型例子是 2004 年能源交易巨头安然公司的倒闭，该公司的经理们利用经济激励来激励销售人员实现特定的收入目标。施韦策说，问题在于实际交易没有盈利。

paragraphs.sourceText: Other studies have shown that saddling employees with unrealistic goals can compel them to lie, cheat or steal. Such was the case in the early 1990s when Sears imposed a sales quota on its auto repair staff. It prompted employees to overcharge for work and to complete unnecessary repairs on a companywide basis. 13 / 39
paragraphs.translationZh: 其他研究表明，让员工背负不切实际的目标可能会迫使他们撒谎、欺骗或偷窃。 20 世纪 90 年代初的情况就是这样，当时西尔斯对其汽车维修人员实行了销售配额。它促使员工收取过高的工作费用，并在全公司范围内完成不必要的维修。

paragraphs.sourceText: Schweitzer concedes his research runs counter to a very large body of literature that commends the many benefits of goal-setting. Advocates of the practice have taken issue with his team’s use of such evidence as news accounts to support his conclusion that goal-setting is widely over-prescribed
paragraphs.translationZh: 施韦策承认他的研究与大量赞扬目标设定的许多好处的文献背道而驰。这种做法的倡导者对他的团队使用新闻报道等证据来支持他的结论（即目标设定普遍被过度规定）提出了质疑

paragraphs.sourceText: In a rebuttal ( 反驳) paper, Dr. Edwin Locke writes:“Goal-setting is not going away. Organizations cannot thrive without being focused on their desired end results any more than an individual can thrive without goals to provide a sense of purpose.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 埃德温·洛克博士在一篇反驳论文中写道：“目标设定不会消失。如果不专注于其期望的最终结果，组织就无法蓬勃发展，就像个人如果没有目标来提供使命感一样，也无法蓬勃发展。”

paragraphs.sourceText: But Schweitzer contends the “mounting causal evidence” linking goal-setting and harmful behavior should be studied to help spotlight issues that merit caution and further investigation. “Even a few negative effects could be so large that they outweigh many positive effects,” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但施韦策认为，应该研究将目标设定和有害行为联系起来的“越来越多的因果证据”，以帮助关注值得谨慎和进一步调查的问题。 “即使是一些负面影响也可能大到超过许多积极影响，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Goal-setting does help coordinate and motivate people. My idea would be to combine that with careful oversight, a strong organizational culture, and make sure the goals that you use are going to be constructive and not significantly harm the organization,” Schweitzer says.
paragraphs.translationZh: “目标设定确实有助于协调和激励人们。我的想法是将其与仔细的监督和强大的组织文化结合起来，并确保您使用的目标具有建设性，并且不会对组织造成重大损害，”施韦策说。

paragraphs.sourceText: For most of the 20th century, Asia asked itself what it could learn from the modern, innovating West. Now the question must be reversed. What can the West’s overly indebted and sluggish (经济滞长的) nations learn from a flourishing Asia?
paragraphs.translationZh: 在 20 世纪的大部分时间里，亚洲都在问自己可以向现代创新的西方学习什么。现在问题必须颠倒过来。负债过高且经济停滞的西方国家可以从繁荣的亚洲学到什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: Just a few decades ago, Asia’s two giants were stagnating(停滞不前) under faulty economic ideologies. However, once China began embracing free-market reforms in the 1980s, followed by India in the 1990s, both countries achieved rapid growth. Crucially, as they opened up their markets, they balanced market economy with sensible government direction. As the Indian economist Amartya Sen has wisely said, “The invisible hand of the market has often relied heavily on the visible hand of government.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 就在几十年前，亚洲两大巨头在错误的经济意识形态下停滞不前。然而，中国在 20 世纪 80 年代开始实行自由市场改革，印度也紧随其后，在 90 年代，两国都实现了快速增长。至关重要的是，当他们开放市场时，他们平衡了市场经济与明智的政府指导。正如印度经济学家阿马蒂亚·森（Amartya Sen）明智地说的那样，“市场看不见的手往往严重依赖政府有形的手。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Contrast this middle path with America and Europe, which have each gone ideologically over-board in their own ways. Since the 1980s, America has been increasingly clinging to the ideology of uncontrolled free markets and dismissing the role of government---following Ronald Regan’s idea that “government is not the solution to our problem; government is the problem. “Of course, when the markets came crashing down in 2007, it was decisive government intervention that saved the day. Despite this fact, many Americans are still strongly opposed to “big government.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 将这条中间道路与美国和欧洲进行对比，这两个国家在意识形态上都以自己的方式走得太远了。自 20 世纪 80 年代以来，美国越来越坚持不受控制的自由市场意识形态，并忽视政府的作用——遵循罗纳德·里根的观点：“政府不是我们问题的解决方案；政府才是问题所在。”当然，当 2007 年市场崩溃时，是政府果断干预挽救了局面。尽管如此，许多美国人仍然强烈反对“大政府”。

paragraphs.sourceText: If Americans could only free themselves from their antigovernment doctrine, they would begin to see that the America’s problems are not insoluble. A few sensible federal measures could put the country back on the right path. A simple consumption tax of, say, 5% would significantly reduce the 15 / 39 country’s huge government deficit without damaging productivity. A small gasoline tax would help free America from its dependence on oil imports and create incentives for green energy development. In the same way, a significant reduction of wasteful agricultural subsidies could also lower the deficit. But in order to take advantage of these common-sense solutions, Americans will have to put aside their own attachment to the idea of smaller government and less regulation. American politicians will have to develop the courage to follow what is taught in all American public-policy schools: that there are good taxes and bad taxes. Asian countries have embraced this wisdom, and have built sound long-term fiscal (财政的) policies as a result.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果美国人能够摆脱反政府主义，他们就会开始看到美国的问题并非无法解决。一些明智的联邦措施可以使该国回到正确的道路上。比如说，征收 5% 的简单消费税将显着减少该国巨额政府赤字，而不会损害生产力。小额汽油税将有助于美国摆脱对石油进口的依赖，并为绿色能源发展创造动力。同样，大幅减少浪费性的农业补贴也可以降低赤字。但为了利用这些常识性解决方案，美国人必须放弃自己对小政府和少监管理念的执着。美国政治家必须鼓起勇气遵循所有美国公共政策学校所教授的内容：税收有好税也有坏税。亚洲国家已经接受了这一智慧，并因此制定了健全的长期财政政策。

paragraphs.sourceText: Meanwhile, Europe has fallen prey to a different ideological trap: the belief that European governments would always have infinite resources and could continue borrowing as if there were no tomorrow. Unlike the Americans, who felt that the markets knew best, the Europeans failed to anticipate how the markets would react to their endless borrowing. Today, the European Union is creating a $580 billion fund to ward off sovereign collapse. This will buy the EU time, but it will not solve the bloc’s larger problem.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与此同时，欧洲陷入了另一个意识形态陷阱：相信欧洲政府将永远拥有无限的资源，并且可以继续借贷，就好像没有明天一样。与认为市场最了解情况的美国人不同，欧洲人未能预料到市场将如何应对他们无休无止的借贷。如今，欧盟正在设立一个 5800 亿美元的基金来防止主权崩溃。这将为欧盟争取时间，但无法解决欧盟更大的问题。
